parameters.content:
## 📄 Email Body Preparation

Renders the email's subject, sender, date, and body into a minimal PDF.

## 📬 Watch for Labeled Emails

Polls Gmail every minute for new messages with the `Events` label applied.

**What to label:**
Any confirmation email you want auto-added to your calendar – flight bookings, hotel reservations, restaurant bookings, doctor appointments, package deliveries, event tickets.

## 📎 Explode Attachments

Splits Gmail attachments into one item per PDF/image so the Extractor can process each one independently.

**Filter:**
Only `application/pdf` and `image/*` types pass through. Inline signatures, calendar invites (.ics), and other formats are skipped.

**Output:**
0+ items, each with the binary under `binary.attachment`

## 🤖 Extract from Email Body

Runs the easybits Extractor on the email body PDF.

Returns extracted data under `json.data`. Fields not found return `null` – a confident "not present" signal we use downstream.

## 🤖 Extract from Attachment

Runs the easybits Extractor on each attached PDF or image.

Same pipeline as "Extracotr: Email Body", different input source. The merge step combines results.

## 🔀 Merge Extractions

Combines extractions from both branches into a single result.

**Priority: Attachments win over body**
Attachments are the authoritative source (the actual ticket/invoice PDF). The body is fallback – used only to fill gaps where the attachment had no value.

**Handles "null" strings:**
Some LLM responses return the literal string `"null"` instead of a JSON `null`. The merge logic treats both as missing values.

## ✅ Validation Gate

Checks if the extraction produced a valid event.

**Required:**
Both `start_datetime` AND `event_type` must be non-empty.

**True branch →** Calendar event creation
**False branch →** Needs-Review flow (no event created, user gets notified)

This is how non-confirmation emails (newsletters, marketing, random replies) get cleanly rejected without producing broken calendar events.

## ✏️ Build Event Description

Constructs the calendar event description from extracted fields.

**Included when present:**
- Vendor name
- Confirmation number
- Participants
- Notes (vendor-specific details)
- Auto-import footer with date

Fields that returned `null` are skipped – the description stays clean and only shows what was actually extracted.

## 📅 Create Calendar Event

Creates the event in your `Auto-imported` Google Calendar.

**Mapped fields:**
- **Summary** ← `title`
- **Start** ← `start_datetime` (ISO 8601 with timezone offset)
- **End** ← `end_datetime`, falls back to `start_datetime` if null
- **Location** ← `location`
- **Description** ← built in previous step

## 🧹 Remove Events Label

Removes the `Events` label from the source email after successful processing.

**Why:**
The Gmail Trigger polls based on the label. Without removal, the next poll would re-process the same email and create duplicate calendar events.

## 🏷️ Flag for Review

Adds the `Events/Needs-Review` label to the email so you can scan all review-needed items in one place in Gmail.

## 🧹 Remove Events Label

Removes the `Events` trigger label from the source email so the next Gmail Trigger poll doesn't reprocess it.

The `Events/Needs-Review` label added in the previous step stays applied – the email remains visible in your `Events/Needs-Review` view in Gmail for manual review.

## 📨 Send Review Notification

Sends an HTML email to yourself with:
- A red "Needs review" header
- The original email's subject and sender
- A list of which fields are missing
- A table of what *was* extracted (so you can tell if it was a near-miss or a total whiff)

**Update:** Change the `sendTo` address in this node to your own email.

# 📅 Email-to-Calendar: Auto-Extract Events from Confirmation Emails with easybits

## What This Workflow Does
Forward any confirmation email – flight bookings, hotel reservations, restaurant bookings, doctor appointments, package deliveries, event tickets – to a labeled inbox, and it automatically becomes a calendar event with all the details (date, time, location, confirmation number, vendor) attached.

One universal pipeline handles every vendor format. No per-airline, per-hotel, per-restaurant parsing logic. The **easybits Extractor** reads the email body and any PDF attachments, pulls out the structured event data, and Google Calendar takes care of the rest.

## How It Works
1. **Gmail Trigger** – Polls Gmail for messages with your chosen label (e.g. `Events`)
2. **Dual Extraction** – Email body is rendered to PDF and extracted; PDF/image attachments are extracted in parallel
3. **Merge** – Combines both extractions; attachment data wins over body data (attachments are authoritative)
4. **Validation Gate** – Confirms a real event was extracted (date + type present)
5. **Calendar Event** – Creates the event in your dedicated `Auto-imported` calendar
6. **Review Path** – Non-confirmation emails get a `Needs-Review` label + email notification listing missing fields

---

## Setup Guide

### 1. Create Your easybits Extractor Pipeline
1. Go to [extractor.easybits.tech](https://extractor.easybits.tech), sign up, and click **"Create a Pipeline"** on your dashboard
2. Fill in the **Pipeline Name** (e.g. "Event Calendar") and **Description**
3. Upload a **sample confirmation email PDF** as your reference (a flight or hotel booking works well)
4. Click **"Auto-Mapping"** – the Extractor analyzes your sample and suggests fields automatically
5. Adjust the suggested fields to match the 9 fields used by this workflow (see field list below)
6. Click **"Save & Test Pipeline"** to verify extraction works
7. Go to **Pipeline Details → View Pipeline** and copy your **Pipeline ID** and **API Key**

**Required fields** (all string type, all should return `null` when missing):
- `event_type` – flight / hotel / restaurant / appointment / delivery / event / other
- `title` – short event summary, max 60 chars
- `start_datetime` – ISO 8601 with timezone offset
- `end_datetime` – ISO 8601 with timezone offset
- `location` – full address or venue name
- `confirmation_number` – booking reference / PNR / order number
- `vendor` – company or service provider
- `notes` – vendor-specific details (seat, table size, room type)
- `participants` – passenger names, party size, attendees

> 💡 **Tip:** The more specific your field descriptions are, the more accurate your results will be – treat them like code.

### 2. Install the easybits Extractor Node
1. The node is **verified** and works on n8n Cloud out of the box – just search for "easybits Extractor" in the node panel
2. For self-hosted instances, go to **Settings → Community Nodes → Install** and enter `@easybits/n8n-nodes-extractor`

### 3. Connect Your Accounts
1. **Gmail** – connect via OAuth2 for the Gmail Trigger and the three Gmail action nodes
2. **Google Calendar** – connect via OAuth2 for the Calendar: Create Event node
3. **easybits Extractor** – paste your Pipeline ID and API Key into both Extractor nodes

### 4. Configure Gmail Labels
1. In Gmail, create a label named `Events` – this is what the trigger watches for
2. Create a nested label `Events/Needs-Review` – emails that fail validation get moved here
3. In n8n, select these labels in the Gmail Trigger, Flag for Review, and Remove Events Label nodes

### 5. Set Up the Auto-Imported Calendar
1. Go to [calendar.google.com](https://calendar.google.com) → "Other calendars" → **+** → Create new calendar
2. Name it `Auto-imported` (or your choice) and save
3. In the Calendar: Create Event node, select this calendar from the dropdown

### 6. Activate & Test
1. Click **Active** in the top-right corner of n8n
2. Apply the `Events` label to any confirmation email in Gmail
3. Within a minute, check your `Auto-imported` calendar – the event should appear with full details
4. The `Events` label is automatically removed after processing to prevent duplicates
